summary: Hold. As written the run cannot build the stack: prepare reaches 166.9 s before the fine phase and the 200 s pre-build deadline lets only one ~42 s nvcc build start, so the result would repeat either the parent or the already-queued standalone experts-rega-w13-fast-silu-epilogue. The fine-N half also shows no gain in the parent's own scored profile at turn_4, the only class where it ran.
justification: The parent's in-prepare gate passed at high (pop 0.961/0.969, random 0.920, bit-exact), but the scored profile of the same job shows no transfer: sliding turn_4 rega_kernel_fine<true>/<false> 734.3+362.3 = 1096.6 us vs master 741.2+357.3 = 1098.5 (73b40cd1) and 1098.3 (d00770b6); full turn_4 1106.3 vs 1133.9 / 1051.8, inside run-to-run spread. The judge-run w13 (741 us) sits between the gate's random 509 and pop 863, so its nbk histogram and L2 state differ from both. The parent's scored configuration was already fine=ON at high only, so the fine-N half repeats it. The fast-silu half is plausible (~2-3% of w13) but is exactly the queued, untested experts-rega-w13-fast-silu-epilogue. Budget: '[rega-lo] prepare total 166.9s' then 'phase 44.3s (build 41.7s) prepare total 211.2s'; REGA_FINE_START_DEADLINE_S 200: whichever module builds first ends near 209 s and every later build is skipped; part (3) can never run.
confounders: combo-b's low-class re-gate decides rega_low_variant per run (ratios near 1), so fast silu at turn_1 depends on it: read the [rega-lo] PATH CHOSEN line.
combo-a normgather slab layout: low concern (same base as parent).
experts-turn-rega-s4-* define the bucket schedule and silu epilogue both edits modify: a build hazard for asserted edits.
align-two-phase-all-t-rega decides chunk counts (nbk histogram) and is part of the 166.9 s pre-phase prepare.
interference: No companion fixes this; run experts-rega-w13-fast-silu-epilogue first and alone. If it routes ON at high and moves turn_4 w13 in the scored profile, a re-mint can stack it with fine-N only as ONE load_inline module (one nvcc call, starting by ~170 s), with a judge-like turn_4 nbk histogram and a warm-L2 graph-replay pair to explain why the parent's gate gain showed as ~0 us scored.
rules_flags: None blocking; fp32 __expf / __frcp_rn with a single bf16 rounding, bounded by the rel L2 and fp64 gates.
Prepare's 300 s limit is the real hazard; any concurrent-build design must use threads around load_inline, not new Python processes.
open_questions: Why did the parent's high-class gate give no scored change at turn_4: judge histogram dominated by full 8-block chunks, or a cold-L2 gate overstating a saving that vanishes with warm L2?
Can both edits compile into one .so, and what is its build time vs the ~130 s left?
Has combo-b's low re-gate chosen V64 in any recent run (fast silu would be excluded at turn_1)?
